correctness.rationale: Expanding each sampled coordinate error update gives exact conditional Euclidean and physical-residual second moments, then positive definiteness yields the sharp one-step windows, with equality and outside-boundary witnesses. In the Hadamard two-mode case, direct sign averaging gives an exact nonnegative two-state second-moment recursion. A subunit coefficient sum and error monotonicity give the strict ratio <2; a contrast-dependent horizon k=floor(sqrt(rho)) attains ratio 2 in the limit. Exact-rational direct sampling and all-path tests corroborate 370 finite cases, but the infinite statements rely on the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: The problem is motivated by comparing expected squared solution error and the physical squared residual, both natural monitored quantities in iterative inverse problems. Their exact sharp step windows separate even for flat orthogonal-column systems, where one might expect them to coincide, and an error-optimal step can generate a genuine large transient in the residual. The sharp factor two, its constructive limiting regime, and exact spectral thresholds support method assessment and numerical stopping diagnostics. No unproved general noisy inverse-problem extension is claimed.
